entries.test: Public commissioning records and operating-capacity disclosures would establish whether any completed data center campus reached 1GW by May 12, 2026.
entries.note: The post explicitly includes campuses within its definition.

entries.test: Abilene commissioning records, equipment inventories and power disclosures would establish the operational buildings and their critical IT loads at publication.
entries.note: The surrounding text supports interpreting the first two buildings as operational.
The claim concerns the private intention behind the descriptions, beyond whether those descriptions were inaccurate.

entries.test: Public commissioning and capacity records would establish whether evidence documented more than a few hundred megawatts of Microsoft capacity coming online in the relevant period.
entries.note: “I can find no evidence” becomes the stronger assertion that no evidence exists.

entries.test: Completion records for Microsoft's publicly announced or documented projects would establish the proportion of their capacity unfinished at publication.
entries.note: “Most” weakens “the vast majority.” The probability hedge concerns the explanation for Microsoft's silence.
“Serious doubts” expresses uncertainty rather than a firm denial.

entries.test: Fairwater Wisconsin commissioning and operating-power records would establish whether running capacity exceeded approximately 117MW at publication.
Building completion records and capacity permits for both Fairwater sites would test the approximately 342MW combined estimate under the stated assumptions.
entries.note: This is an assumption-based estimate of completed capacity, not eventual campus capacity.

entries.test: Microsoft's documented capacity additions over the preceding six months and the Fairwater capacity estimate would establish whether the claimed addition was approximately six times that estimate.
entries.note: The following “I'm calling bullshit” supports the included rejection.
He questions the construction claim. “There is no trace” strengthens his report that he cannot find one.

entries.test: Public announcements and commissioning records for Microsoft projects announced during the preceding three years would test the claimed absence of documented operational sites beyond the two Fairwaters.
entries.note: This describes the result of his research, not an unequivocal claim that no other site exists.
The normalization strengthens his inability to account for capacity into a conclusion about capacity. The compound claim also attributes deliberate concealment.

entries.test: Microsoft's quarterly commissioning and active-capacity records would establish whether it brought roughly 1GW online in each of the two referenced quarters.
entries.note: “It obviously hasn't” supplies an assertion after the rhetorical question.

entries.test: Public groundbreaking and opening dates across data center projects would establish documented completions and typical construction durations.
entries.note: His finding only a few confirmed openings does not mean only a few can be confirmed. The normalization also removes “it appears.”

entries.test: Public construction updates for the projects identified in the article would establish how many remained unfinished years after groundbreaking.
entries.note: “Most” weakens “the vast majority,” and the normalization drops his claim that most are specifically still under construction.

entries.test: Project-level groundbreaking, completion and original schedule records would establish construction durations and whether larger projects miss schedules more often.
entries.note: The source describes a general pattern rather than explicitly asserting causation. The normalization removes “seems.”
The proposed causal explanation is explicitly “most likely.”

entries.test: Publicly claimed capacity additions compared with documented commissioning and operating capacity would test the alleged mismatch.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives “rapid buildout” a concrete capacity-and-completion meaning.

entries.test: Public shipment totals, customer deployment disclosures and inventory records would establish whether most shipped Blackwell GPUs remained unused in warehouses at publication.
entries.note: In context, this is an emphatic substantive assertion about deployment.

entries.test: Public customer deployment counts and operational cluster inventories would establish whether more than approximately one million Blackwell GPUs were in service at publication.

entries.note: The source says an illusion of utility, availability and viability, not demand. It also specifies helping selected partners install current-generation hardware.
“I'd be surprised” makes the capacity estimate probabilistic.

entries.test: AI data center project completion records and groundbreaking-to-opening dates would establish whether most remained unfinished and completed smaller builds took two to three years.
entries.note: The deal is offered as evidence of the asserted industry conditions.

entries.test: Quarterly commissioning records and usable AI compute power disclosures would establish whether additions exceeded a few hundred megawatts per quarter around publication.
entries.note: “I think in reality” introduces his substantive estimate.

entries.test: Microsoft's active-capacity additions during the six months before publication would establish whether approximately 2GW came online.
Public construction, commissioning and operating-power records would establish whether the discussed AI capacity was coming online at publication.
entries.note: Read in context as a claim about the discussed buildout, not a denial that any capacity exists.
“Stinks of desperation” is an evaluative characterization; “shows” turns it into a firmer inference.
The financial effect is testable, but the compound assertion includes deliberately worsening margins as a private intention.

entries.test: Microsoft's AI revenue breakdown and growth contributions from OpenAI and Microsoft 365 Copilot would establish their shares of the stated run rate and its increases.
entries.note: “Only ever seems to expand” becomes the firmer “grows only.”
The explanation is explicitly qualified by “likely.”
“Far more likely” marks a probabilistic explanation.

entries.test: Hyperscaler capacity additions and realized revenue under the cited Anthropic and OpenAI contracts would establish whether those revenues materialized despite persistently limited additions.
entries.note: No deadline is supplied for the conditional revenue outcome.

entries.test: Public capacity additions, utilization, unmet orders and demand data would test whether limited supply explains the asserted insatiable-demand narrative.
entries.note: The source says the narrative results from limited capacity; the normalization substitutes apparent shortages as the effect.

entries.test: The delivery records and capacity figures for projects documented in his research would establish the total capacity he identified for the preceding two years.
entries.note: The scope is his documented findings, not all worldwide deliveries.

entries.test: Disclosures of uninstalled GPU assets, subsequent deployment and depreciation expenses would establish whether the stated inventory conditions produce a substantial depreciation increase.
entries.note: The four named hyperscalers provide the contextual scope.
This particular statement expresses doubt rather than a firm denial.
“Seeing value” has no agreed financial meaning here. The normalization also substitutes NVIDIA for Jensen Huang.
“Anything untoward” is broader than bad faith. The claim also concerns builders' private prior understanding of construction difficulty.

entries.test: Construction pace and full commissioning dates would establish whether Abilene finishes around mid-2027 and the other Oracle projects no earlier than 2030 if the stated pace continues.
entries.note: “At this rate” is a condition. “Not before mid-2027” broadens his stated mid-2027 completion estimate.
The forecast is conditional on construction and explicitly qualified by “likely.”

entries.test: Oracle's segment profits, revenue growth and GPU compute margins would establish the profitability and growth of its existing businesses relative to its data center commitments.
entries.note: The normalization omits the specific negative-100% margin and strengthens the comparison into having no large profitable business.

entries.test: Anthropic's capacity utilization, service restrictions and subscription economics would establish whether it continues hitting capacity limits while subsidizing users.
entries.note: The present-tense assertion loses “suggests.” The continued-capacity forecast uses firm “will” language.

entries.test: Public evidence of OpenAI capacity restrictions tied to delayed data center construction would establish the predicted outcome.
entries.note: “Eventually” supplies no deadline; slow construction is the asserted cause, not a stated hypothetical antecedent.

entries.test: AI labs' inference revenues and costs, together with training-versus-inference compute allocations, would test the two rejected propositions.
entries.note: Whether the purchase supports his inference is separate from whether the underlying claims are testable.

entries.test: Public commissioning, capacity and retrofit records for each hyperscaler since 2023 would establish documented additions and their sources.
entries.note: “I can find no compelling evidence” becomes an unrestricted evidence claim. “Mainly” is also added to the retrofit assertion.

entries.test: Groundbreaking and completion dates for facilities above 50MW, plus commissioning records for 1GW campuses, would test both assertions as of publication.

entries.note: “Severely doubt” makes this an uncertain prediction despite its insulting wording.
This is advice about how readers should interpret announced schedules.

entries.test: Public completion rates, NVIDIA shipment totals and deployed GPU inventories would establish whether the stated low-completion condition corresponds to years of uninstalled chip supply.
entries.note: The normalization turns “if that's true” into an unconditional inference.

entries.test: Public installation inventories and customer deployment disclosures would establish whether fewer than 1.5 million of the referenced Blackwell GPUs had been installed at publication.
entries.note: The emphatic refusal expresses a substantive deployment claim.
“Probably” is explicit. The normalization omits the absence of guidance on when remaining construction will finish.

entries.test: Public construction and full-completion records across the relevant data center projects would establish whether most remained only partly built.
entries.note: The judgment “bad” is separable from the extracted factual industry claim.
He asserts a mismatch, but specifies no shared test for financials being “disconnected” from infrastructure.
The normalization replaces the largest-ever comparison with a claim about the proportion of NVIDIA sales. “Might” explicitly marks possibility.
“Only as viable” provides no agreed outcome for comparing corporate futures with construction projects.

entries.test: Project abandonment records, unrecovered investment totals and financing disclosures would establish whether failed construction leaves hundreds of billions lost with substantial pension- and insurance-funded private credit exposure.
entries.note: “Wasted” has a concrete financial-loss reading in this context.
